memoryText: If my people who are called by my name humble themselves, and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and will forgive their sin and heal their land.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 2 Chronicles 7:14 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is one of the most quoted verses in the Old Testament, and it is easy to misuse. So begin with its setting. God is speaking to Solomon, at night, after the temple is dedicated. He is speaking about Israel, the land, and the temple. In its original context, the “land” is the land of Israel. We should not simply apply it to any modern nation, but we can learn the pattern, which is repeated across Scripture.

“If my people who are called by my name.” The promise is for a particular people: those who bear God’s name. The church is also called by his name. God’s concern is first with his own people.

“Humble themselves.” This is the first step. The problem is not mainly outside; it begins with pride. Humility is the beginning of any restoration.

“And pray and seek my face.” Prayer is asking. To seek his face is to want God himself, not just his gifts. It is looking for his presence and his favor.

“And turn from their wicked ways.” Repentance is not only sorrow but change. There is a turning around.

“Then I will hear from heaven and will forgive their sin and heal their land.” God’s response is threefold: he hears, he forgives, and he heals. Every verb is his gift. We do not heal the land; he does. Our part is to humble, pray, seek, and turn.

Remember that this passage was fulfilled in part under Hezekiah and Josiah. It points toward the greater turning that Christ makes possible. Pray this verse for your church first, then for your community. Begin with yourself.
weekInReview: This week you read the end of David’s reign and the beginning of Solomon’s according to the Chronicler. You heard David’s charge to Solomon, “Know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart,” and his great prayer, “All things come from you, and of your own have we given you.” You watched Solomon ask for wisdom, build the temple on Mount Moriah, and dedicate it as God’s glory filled the house. You heard God’s answer to Solomon’s prayer in 7:14. In Psalm 132, you read the two oaths, David’s to God and God’s to David. In Psalms 135 and 136, you sang the songs of the second temple: the God who chose Israel, who is above all idols, and whose steadfast love endures forever.
reflectionQuestions: David said, “All things come from you, and of your own have we given you.” How does that change the way you think about your money, time, and talents?
2 Chronicles 7:14 gives four responses: humble, pray, seek, turn. Which is hardest for you right now?
Solomon’s temple is fulfilled in Jesus and in his people. How does it change your daily life to know that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
prayerPrompts: Humble yourself before God and ask him to hear from heaven.
Ask him to forgive sin and heal what is broken.
Thank him for Christ, the true temple.
